claims.statement: From 18 February 2027, the EU Batteries Regulation requires an electronic battery passport for each light-means-of-transport battery, EV battery and industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the market or put into service.

The regulation provides legitimate-interest access to specified information for repairers, remanufacturers, second-life operators and recyclers, including state of health, status and some usage history, subject to role and purpose limits.
Hypothesis: installers will trade first-look rights for a safer zero-inventory disposition service; future feedstock volume, residual values and buyer demand are unvalidated.

contrary_evidence: The Batteries Regulation restricts commercially sensitive passport access and forbids an authorized storage or processing operator from reusing passport data beyond the contracted service.
The regulation requires permitted facilities for waste-battery treatment; a software broker cannot lawfully treat or casually transport waste batteries.

economics.acquisition_route: Secure prospective first-notice agreements from five installers, then dry-run documentation on ten known future retirement events with a permitted recycler and one qualified second-life buyer.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated path: 2,500 annual unit or batch dispositions at PLN 2,500 average net revenue would yield PLN 6.25m revenue; 25% operating profit and a 4x value imply PLN 6.25m enterprise value and PLN 5m for an 80% founder stake. Achieving this in 8-10 years requires national installer contracts and repeatable compliance economics.
economics.founder_time: 10-16 hours per week for data schema, routing decisions and partner management; hazardous-goods logistics and testing remain with credentialed partners.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated estimate: 35-55% after testing, insurance, specialist legal review and licensed logistics; no inventory purchases or physical treatment are included in the initial model.
economics.payback: Unvalidated target: 18-30 months at 12-20 commercial-unit or batch dispositions per month; payback could be much longer if most units are low-value waste.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: PLN 500-2,500 owner-side documentation/inspection fee per commercial unit or module batch plus 8-15% of a completed non-waste resale or a fixed compliant-routing fee.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Installers generate recurring replacement flow; buyers return if classification, state-of-health evidence and delivery quality are dependable.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: forward feedstock visibility and a longitudinal map from battery condition to realized route improve pricing and buyer confidence while avoiding speculative inventory
fingerprint.customer: commercial battery owners and solar or storage installers needing a safe retirement route, with second-life operators, remanufacturers and recyclers as buyers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: embed first-notice clauses into maintenance and repowering contracts through installers, then build buyer routes with permitted recyclers and qualified second-life firms
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: first-look intake, passport and document check, partner testing, compliant buyer matching and auditable handoff sold as per-unit service and success fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the owner pays a chain-of-custody and inspection fee, while a qualified buyer pays a disclosed brokerage fee only after accepting a classified unit or batch
fingerprint.problem_trigger: warranty replacement, site repowering, lease end, capacity fade or an insurer requiring documented disposition

founder_fit: Combines battery-health data, renewable-sector access and quantitative residual-value decisions.
The no-inventory pilot limits downside within available capital.
Installer contracts can create recurring supply without consumer brand building.
AI can assist document matching and state-of-health triage while safety decisions remain expert-led.
risks: A battery classified as waste can trigger strict storage, transport, treatment and cross-border rules.
Fire, injury, environmental and chain-of-custody liability can exceed transaction revenue.
Battery-passport access is role-based and does not grant unrestricted commercial reuse of data.
Residual values may collapse as new battery prices and chemistries change.

structure.control_point: contractual first-notice and first-inspection rights over future retired batteries plus permissioned condition and disposition records
structure.critical_dependency: each battery must have a lawful, safe route and buyers must value tested residual life enough to cover logistics, compliance and brokerage

thesis: Sign installers and commercial battery owners to first-notice and right-of-first-inspection agreements for warranty replacements, repowering and retirement events. Use lawful battery-passport access and independent testing partners to route each unit to continued use, repurposing, remanufacturing or permitted recycling, earning inspection and brokerage fees without initially taking title or holding inventory. The defensible asset would be contracted feedstock visibility and disposition history, but product-versus-waste status must be decided by qualified counsel and permitted operators for every route.
title: First-Look Exchange for Retired Commercial Batteries
uncertainties: How many commercial batteries will reach an actionable retirement event in the first three years?
Which passport fields and diagnostic interfaces will legitimately be available to the proposed operator?
What testing cost separates reusable products from waste safely and defensibly?
Will installers grant first-look rights without demanding an upfront guarantee or floor price?
